slides.heading: Changing Variable Values
slides.body: Changing Variable Values is part of Variables and Primitive Data Types. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Changing Variable Values
slides.body: A variable can be assigned a new value. When this happens, the old value is replaced by the new value.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: Changing a variable is like updating a whiteboard. The new information replaces what was written before.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Use clear variable names and match the data type to the kind of value you need to store.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Create a variable named level, change it to a new value, then print it.
slides.hint: Assign level again using a new value before printing.

coding_challenge.prompt_text: Set coins to 5, update it to 8, and print the final value.
coding_challenge.hint_text: Use the idea from the lesson. Keep the code short, readable, and correctly indented.
